subject: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation for Dedicated commitment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@opsly.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation for Dedicated commitment

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. To finalize sizing for the Dedicated commitment (OPSLY-2028-10-M1) we need a short telemetry sample and a few clarifications so our capacity model can produce an accurate GPU allocation and burst plan. Could you attach the last 7 days of request-level telemetry (CSV) or a small sample that includes these columns: timestamp, route, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, latency_ms, success/failure, session_id (if applicable), and model_tag?

If easier, a quick answers table will work too. Key items we care about:
- Steady-state rps and peak 5‑min rps
- Typical prompt vs. response token distribution (median / p95)
- Percent of requests that rely on KV cache/session affinity
- Burst windows you expect (days of week / hours / event types)
- P99 latency SLO target for user-facing routes (ms)

I attached a one‑page example CSV layout and a short questionnaire to fill. Once we have the sample, I’ll run a quick occupancy/latency simulation and share a recommended GPU mix + canary rollout plan.

Thanks —
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Attachments: sizing_sample_template.csv (attachment)

From: Priya Shah <priya@opsly.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Jeffrey Klein <jeff@opsly.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation for Dedicated commitment

Hi Marcus —

Thanks — attaching a 7‑day sample (opsly_traffic_sample.csv) and a short KPI snapshot (opsly_kpi_snapshot.pdf). Quick highlights from the sample:
- Steady-state: ~45 rps average across all routes
- Peak 5‑min: 1,150 rps during marketing campaigns (observed between 11:30–11:45 PST on weekdays)
- Prompt tokens: median 18, p95 120
- Response tokens: median 64, p95 540 (long-form answers during support flows)
- ~22% of requests have session affinity / KV cache hits
- Target p99: 300 ms for interactive routes; 750 ms acceptable for background batch-type flows

Notes: We have two primary routes — interactive-search (user-facing) and async-summary (background). During product launches the async-summary spikes concurrently with interactive traffic (same event).

Let me know if the CSV columns need reshaping. We can also export a 1‑hour trace if that helps.

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform — Opsly Inc
priya@opsly.ai

Attachments: opsly_traffic_sample.csv (attachment), opsly_kpi_snapshot.pdf (attachment)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@opsly.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 08:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation for Dedicated commitment

Thanks Priya — this is perfect. A few clarifying questions before I run the occupancy sim: 

1) For the response p95 of 540 tokens, is that dominated by a single route (async-summary) or spread across both? If the async-summary is the heavy tail, can you share the % of total tokens from that route?
2) For session affinity: is the KV cache hit rate measured on identical prompt prefixes, or at session start (i.e., same conversation id)? Any approximation of average KV cache entry size (tokens) helps.
3) Do you use model variants depending on route (e.g., smaller embedding/light model for search, larger for summary)? If so, please map route->model_tag used in your sample.
4) What is your preferred availability tradeoff? We can size for lower cost with graceful fallback to a smaller variant, or for strict SLO with dedicated overprovision. Which approach do you prefer for launch 1?

If you can reply inline, I’ll produce two options: (A) cost‑optimized with tiered fallbacks and (B) SLO‑first with headroom and burst reserve. Plan to send the simulation by EOD Thursday.

—Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation — internal note

Internal note for sizing:

- Given the sample, recommend a mixed fleet: 60% A100‑like instances (for async-summary heavy tails), 40% H200-equivalent (for low-latency interactive path) with quantized 4-bit variants on background jobs to reduce cost.
- Plan: reserve a 20% burst buffer (hot spare GPUs) for campaign windows, and configure automatic fallback routing to a smaller model family for non-interactive routes.
- KV cache: assume 20–25% effective hit rate; add a small memcached cluster recommendation in the handoff doc.
- Ops: propose a canary over 48 hours with traffic ramping 10→50→100% of production routes. Include a rollback policy that falls back to a hosted small‑model endpoint for <5 min grace.

Marissa
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

(Forwarded inline from Marcus's exchange with Opsly)

From: Priya Shah <priya@opsly.ai>

Cc: Jeffrey Klein <jeff@opsly.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Oct 2028 17:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inference load heuristics & burst annotation for Dedicated commitment

Hi Marcus —

Replying inline to your questions:
1) The 540 token p95 is ~85% async-summary; interactive-search p95 is ~200 tokens. Async-summary accounts for ~28% of total tokens but only 12% of rps.
2) KV cache: measured on session_id; average cached prefix ~120 tokens; hit rate ~22% as sampled.
3) Route→model mapping: interactive-search -> redwood-search-v1 (smaller); async-summary -> redwood-gen-large-v2 (full); fallback path uses redwood-gen-medium-q4. Model_tags are present in the CSV under "model_tag" column.
4) For launch 1 we prefer SLO‑first with headroom; we can accept extra cost in month 1 for stability and tune later.

Next steps: please share the two simulation options and a recommended reserved capacity commitment (monthly GPU count and burst quota). Also — can we schedule a 30‑minute sync Thursday to review the canary plan? Our team is available 10–12 PST.

Thanks —
Priya
Opsly Inc
